summary: Investigated why registry-installed skills could not be viewed or edited, found they were classified as non-editable because they live in a junction-linked Git clone outside managed skill roots, which also blocked selection in the UI. Implemented read-only viewing of registry skills via a new server handler with symlink rejection, refactored the Skills settings UI to add a sort control (Name / Status / Source) with a flat list, replacing the earlier two-group split.
decisions: Registry skills are intentionally not editable because they are junction-linked from a Git clone and editing would conflict with updates; the UI was also blocking selection, which is unnecessarily restrictive.
All skills should be viewable; registry skills stay read-only, and editing requires forking the skill into a managed skills directory.
Server writes must reject symlinked/junction-backed skill files to avoid modifying the registry checkout.

Replaced the two-group ('Your skills' / 'Extension skills') split with a single flat list plus an explicit sort selector (Name, Status, Source) after the group buckets proved too uneven (4 vs 80 skills).
errors: svelte-check failed after introducing .toSorted because the target lib was older than ES2023; resolved by switching back to Array.prototype.sort with an explicit comparator and typing the comparator parameters.
